title: Generating phenotypic decline indexes using the pdi package
text: Oak declines complex disease syndromes consist many visual indicators include aspects tree size, crown condition trunk condition (Denman Webber 2009; Denman et al. 2014). can cause difficulty manual classification symptomatic non-symptomatic trees reality broad spectrum oak tree health condition. Two oak decline indexes developed quantitatively describe differentiate oak decline syndromes Quercus robur. include: Phenotypic Decline Index (PDI) - measure overall decline severity, scoring trees 0 1. severely declining oak trees score closer 1. Decline Acuteness Index (DAI) - measure differentiate Chronic Oak Decline (COD) Acute Oak Decline score -1 1. Acutely declining trees score closer 1 chronically declining trees score closer -1. information methodology behind generating decline indexes, see article: Finch, J.P., Brown, N., Beckmann, M., Denman, S. Draper, J., 2021. Index measures oak decline severity using phenotypic descriptors. Forest Ecology Management, 485, p.118948. vignette provide example framework generate decline indexes based machine learning algorithm random forest, using example set phenotypic descriptors. begin, load package: following example example also make use dplyr package data manipulation, ggplot2 visualisation pipe (%>%) magrittr package. additionally required packages can loaded using:

title: Generating phenotypic decline indexes using the pdi package
text: Additional composite descriptors can calculated account three dimensional tree attributes covariate nature certain descriptors. additional descriptors provided pdi include: liveCrownRatio - Live crown ratio (%) crownCondition - Crown condition (%) crownVolume - Crown volume (m3) bleedPrevalence - Bleed prevalence (%) agrilusExitHoleDensity - Agrilus exit hole density (m-2) descriptors can calculated example data using:
code: a <- sa %>%   mutate(`Live crown ratio (%)` = liveCrownRatio(`Total height (m)`,                                                  `Lower crown height (m)`),          `Crown condition (%)` = crownCondition(`Missing crown (%)`,                                                 `Crown transparency (%)`),          `Crown volume (m^3)` = crownVolume(`Crown radius (m)`,                                             `Total height (m)`,                                             `Lower crown height (m)`,                                             `Crown condition (%)`),          `Bleed prevalence (%)` = bleedPrevalence(`Active bleed length (mm)`,                                                   `Active bleeds`,                                                   `Black staining length (mm)`,                                                   `Black staining`,                                                   `Diameter at breast height (m)`),          `Agrilus exit hole density (m^-2)` = agrilusExitHoleDensity(`Agrilus exit holes`,                                                                      `Diameter at breast height (m)`)   )

text: Now decline indexes calculated, next need understand relative contributions descriptors indexes. can calculated using mean decrease accuracy variable importance metric fitted random forest models. importance scores can retrieved using following: relative descriptor contributions can plotted using following code, higher contributing descriptors top y-axis.  can seen plot , crown volume descriptor ranked highest therefore contributed calculated decline indexes. plot blow shows crown volume plotted calculated PDI values tree. can seen trees lower PDI values (healthier) also greater crown volumes expected.  important stage carefully assess descriptor contributions , associations , calculated decline indexes ensure suitably describe decline syndromes based. achieved, solutions include using supervised random forest models instead unsupervised approach used addition/removal phenotypic descriptors models.
code: descriptor_contributions <- m %>%   descriptorContributions() descriptor_contributions %>%   arrange(MeanDecreaseAccuracy) %>%   mutate(Descriptor = factor(Descriptor,levels = Descriptor)) %>%   ggplot(aes(x = MeanDecreaseAccuracy,y = Descriptor)) +   geom_point() +   theme_bw() DIs %>%   bind_cols(a %>%               select(`Crown volume (m^3)`)) %>%   ggplot(aes(x = PDI,y = `Crown volume (m^3)`)) +   geom_point() +   theme_bw()
